answer: Each identity locks an 80-credit bond at its own wharf, then faces a lottery audit each epoch. A falcon panel draws 4% of identities, checks work and funding, and any draw audits that funding cluster. The first fake risks 80 credits, but each added fake raises the chance one draw exposes the cluster, so expected loss rises faster than linearly. Renting wallets fails: the prism check splits records into work and funding strands, and reused payouts re-link rentals, forfeiting all bonds. One thousand fakes lock 80,000 credits, while an honest agent locks one bond and keeps it.
